source_read: PDF pp. 1503-1505 (PDFs/MDMA/Mithoefer_2003_ScienceCorrespondence.pdf): the letter (p. 1504, one paragraph, 16 references) and the reply (pp. 1504-1505, five paragraphs, 15 references) read in full, with p. 1504 rendered at 110 dpi to count the reply's paragraphs. The unrelated letters on pp. 1503 and 1505 were not used. The CSF statement checked against McCann et al. (1994), PDF pp. 132-133 and Table 4.

design.note: An exchange of letters, carded as one item because the letter and the reply share pages and a DOI; narrative-review plus design_detail is the workable label. I confirmed the structure on the rendered page: one paragraph for the letter, five for the reply.

instrument.note: none-applicable (editors' narrative-review checklist) for the exchange as a whole.

key_findings.note: Letter, left column: rare deaths in people, high mortality in the primates, the regimen therefore not a common recreational one, and the interspecies scaling model questioned, with the earlier squirrel-monkey report cited as inconsistent.
Letter, middle of the paragraph; references 7-9 are the two imaging reports and the post-mortem case, and 10-12 the CSF studies. Reference 11 is McCann et al. (1994), the paper carded in this batch.
Letter, end of the paragraph; reference 14 is a New Scientist news-service item and reference 16 a conference presentation.

Reply, 1st paragraph: interspecies scaling not used in these studies, one of ten monkeys dead of complications related to hyperthermia, conclusions about mortality premature given the sample size, isolated human deaths with hyperthermia, and the rise from 500 emergency-room visits in 1994 to about 4500 in 2000.

Reply, 3rd paragraph (right column), verified on the rendered page: mouse findings, the dosing-pattern observation, heterogeneous groups, dopamine transporter not expected to differ, and CSF HVA neither sensitive nor specific.
Reply, 4th paragraph, running from the foot of p. 1504 onto p. 1505.
Reply, 5th paragraph (p. 1505, left column): the conference presentation, the exchange of letters on interspecies scaling, and the Phase I study in which no neurotoxicity measures were taken.

reporting_issues.note: McCann et al. (1994), Table 4 (p. 133): CSF HVA 19.4 (SD 7.8) ng/ml in 30 people who used MDMA against 27.4 (21.3) in 28 controls; the HVA paragraph (pp. 132-133) gives the ANCOVA with age and height, group F(1,52)=6.9, p=.01, group by gender F(1,52)=4.3, p=.04, with post-hoc differences in women and not in men; the Discussion (p. 135) says MDMA-exposed women also have reduced CSF HVA. The letter's description fails for this source, and the reply accepts it.
Letter 'high mortality'; reply 'one of ten monkeys'; Barnett and Doblin (2021), p. 2 of the online-first PDF, 'two of them died'. None of the three is the 2002 paper.

Reference 14 is D. Concar, New Scientist News Service online, 28 September 2002; the reply states that none of the three sources cited for toxicity-free clinical research measured neurotoxicity, and reference 16 is a conference paper.

The source side is right: the letter is signed by Mithoefer, Jerome and Doblin and the reply by Ricaurte, Yuan, Hatzidimitriou, Cord and McCann, on shared pages. I did not check the Crossref record itself, which is where the author-list problem arises.

domains.note: some-concerns for balance is right for the exchange taken as a whole, since both positions are printed.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial, and the card is right to record that the reply defended primate data withdrawn three months later.

missed: The route-of-administration exchange is not on the card at all. The letter charges that the group had previously reported subcutaneous injection in squirrel monkeys to be twice as neurotoxic as the oral route (its reference 6), which it says contradicts their present position that the oral route offers little or no protection; the reply (2nd paragraph) answers that all four studies addressing the question are cited, three finding no protective effect and a fourth varying protection by brain region. This is the letter's second charge of internal inconsistency and should be a key finding, reported as a study condition in the animal work and with no administration guidance.

The emergency-room figures in the reply's 1st paragraph (500 visits in 1994, about 4500 in 2000) carry no citation: none of the reply's 15 references is a surveillance source. The card quotes the figures in key finding 3 without recording that they are unsourced.

The reply's 4th paragraph argument moves from methamphetamine to MDMA (reduced dopamine transporters and motor slowing in people who had used methamphetamine, offered as a parallel), which is the only human evidence it brings to the dopamine question and is about a different drug. The card reports the content but does not mark the species-and-drug gap, which matters for cl_mdma_dopamine_human.
